reason: E1 shows that a single-phase solid solution without precipitates has lower strength, and that precipitation-hardened conditions have higher strength, supporting the obstacle premise. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is initially precipitate-free, that aging at 600 °C induces nanoscale precipitates in this specific alloy, or that the predicted property changes occur; these key premises are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is a homogeneous single-phase solid solution without nanoscale precipitates or incipient ordering
Absence of nanoscale obstacles in CoCrFeNiTi allows easy dislocation glide, giving low hardness/strength and high ductility
Nanoscale precipitates or ordered clusters in other HEAs act as dislocation obstacles that increase hardness and strength
Thermal aging at ~600 °C can induce nanoscale precipitates or ordered clusters in CoCrFeNiTi without bulk phase transformation
Induced nanoscale obstacles will increase yield strength and hardness by 20–50% with only modest ductility loss
